messages.author: 0111ed37d2662b85
messages.subject: EnKF + PMCMC for multivariate SSM
parts:
Many thanks to the developers and contributors for all the great work building this useful software.

I am interested in utilizing NIMBLE's ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) in a particle marginal Metropolis Hastings (PMMH) algorithm to fit a state space model (SSM) with unknown parameters. The SSM is multivariate, and the covariance matrix depends on unknown, time-varying parameters that I hope to estimate as part of the model fitting procedure. Finally, the evolutions of the state equation can be non-linear (although both the observation and evolution processes are conditionally Gaussian). As a reference, the model is an example of what Katzfuss, Stroud, and Wikle (2020) call a hierarchical SSM, but with no transformation layer (eqs. 2-4 in their paper).

So far, I've been successful using NIMBLE to create particle filters for my model with fixed parameters, and as I had hoped the EnKF seems to perform better than the bootstrap particle filter. I've taken a swing at the full PMMF with the help of the recent paper by Michaud et al. on arXiv, soon to be published in JSS, but I've hit some snags. Rather than post a MWE, I wanted to start by trying to clarify a few things, and ask whether there might be any existing examples of similar applications that I could use as a guide. (1) From what I read in Section 6.1 of Michaud et al. (2017), it sounds like NIMBLE's PMMH approaches are limited to bootstrap and auxiliary particle filters, and so using an EnKF requires a little extra work (i.e., I can't just create the EnKF using buildEnsembleKF() and then set the control argument pf = EnKF). Is that correct? If so, could you help me understand what steps would be necessary to connect these two pieces in NIMBLE? (2) After a little trial and error, it appears to me that to use a multivariate EnKF, both the latent state vector and the observation vector must be specified as coming from a multivariate Gaussian distribution in the model code. My observation vector is conditionally independent given the latent states (i.e., the covariance for the observation process is diagonal). Is there any way to make use of the conditional independence at the observation level to gain some computational efficiency?

Thanks for your help,
Henry Scharf


Katzfuss, M., Stroud, J. R., & Wikle, C. K. (2020). Ensemble Kalman methods for high-dimensional hierarchical dynamic space-time models. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 115(530), 866-885.

Michaud, N., de Valpine, P., Turek, D., Paciorek, C. J., & Nguyen, D. (2017). Sequential Monte Carlo methods in the nimble R package. arXiv preprint arXiv:1703.06206.

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: EnKF + PMCMC for multivariate SSM
parts:
Hi Henry, this raises a number of interesting questions. Here goes... 

1) You cannot directly use the output of buildEnsembleKF and set pf = EnKF.  The reason is that our particle MCMC requires that the particle filter that it uses must have methods to get and set the last log-likelihood and have access to the mvEWsamples data structure. (For the latter issue, it might simply be a matter of renaming the 'mvSamples' in our ensemble KF to be 'mvEWsamples'.) If you look in the code for sampler_RW_PF or sampler_RW_PF_block in our MCMC_samplers.R file you should be able to see how these are used in the context of the particle MCMC. 

1a) I presume one can get an estimate of the log marginal likelihood  from the ensemble KF or you wouldn't be asking your question, though I'd have to refresh my memory of the algorithm to know how one uses the ensemble KF to estimate the marginal likelihood.

1b) I haven't thought about it carefully, but I'm optimistic that you could take our ensemble KF code (in filtering_enkf.R) and modify it so it has the parts that are needed to use it with our sampler_RW_PF or sampler_RW_PF_block. We'd be happy to answer questions and iterate with you if you wanted to take that on as a project. 

2) As far as what kinds of distributions are allowed, I see our documentation for the ensemble KF could be improved. If you look in enkfScalFunc and enkfMultFunc, you see we expect the distribution to have 'mean' and either 'var' or 'cov' respectively. And if you look in ENKFStep, you'll see that we expect the 'cov' to be a matrix when we create 'kMat'.

2a) If you specify the observations as having a dmnorm distribution and provide "cov" (rather than "prec" or "cholesky") then when the enKF goes to get the "cov" of the observations in getVar() using getParam(), it will just be a direct copy of "cov" out of the model without any matrix algebra involved. So it's a bit inefficient in that the zeroes are copied and then when 'kMat' is created, one is also adding those 0s on the off-diagonal. But it's probably not too much of a cost compared to all the other calculations going on. However, if you need/want to parameterize the dmnorm for your observations using "prec" or "cholesky" rather than "cov" , then under the hood nimble will need to do matrix algebra to construct "cov" and that would be costly if done repeatedly, such as if the "prec" or "cholesky" were functions of unknown parameters. Of course you are probably needing to construct "cov" from scalar variance parameters. It's probably most efficient to do this in a user-defined function, but doing it as a for  loop in the model code directly may not be too inefficient if the length of the vector at each time point is not too long. 

2b) It shouldn't be too hard to modify our enKF to handle other observation distributions. E.g., you could write your own dmnorm_diagonal distribution that is parameterized in terms of a vector of variances. Then in the enKF, you could modify the line for creating 'kMat' so that it takes advantage of the fact that the covariance is diagonal and just uses the vector of variances appropriately.  You'd need to modify the 'returnType' of 'getVar' to be one-dimensional.

Final note: we are in the process of pulling our particle filters out of the main nimble package and into a new package called 'nimbleSMC'. If you dove into this and modified our enKF in ways that would be useful for others, we'd be happy to discuss if it made sense to add your new functionality to that package, with you being a co-author of the package then, of course.

-chris
